project.title: aquascape-wood-orthos-v3-calibrated
project.description: Repair the conflicting wood depth visible in the generated gray three-view study.
project.art_direction: Strict neutral-gray orthographic engineering construction; same-object geometric consistency before material.

brief.name: wood_orthographic_calibrated
brief.description:
Create a corrected MONOCHROME ORTHOGRAPHIC CONSTRUCTION DRAWING of the exact forked wood in the supplied three-view pencil study. Keep the same object identity and branch inventory. The old sheet has a real inconsistency: its TOP view root footprint is much deeper than its RIGHT view is wide. Correct this through physically consistent root/limb geometry. Do not merely copy the old three silhouettes.
Use STANDARD ENGINEERING ALIGNMENT in a square white sheet: TOP in the upper-left quadrant, FRONT in the lower-left quadrant directly beneath TOP, RIGHT in the lower-right quadrant directly beside FRONT. Leave the upper-right quadrant blank. Small plain labels TOP, FRONT, RIGHT. Thin faint straight projection guide lines join shared extents. This layout is essential: TOP and FRONT have exactly the same left and right X coordinates and same printed X width; FRONT and RIGHT share the same top and bottom Y coordinates and same printed height. RIGHT horizontal front-back width equals TOP vertical depth at the SAME UNIFORM SCALE. No separate icon-fit scaling.
Object: knotted thick root crotch on left, long shallow-S main limb to the right, one short upward fork, frayed left root, and two stabilizing root feet spreading in front/back. The roots cannot occupy a deep footprint in TOP while collapsing to an artificially narrow pair of feet in RIGHT. RIGHT must show the entire full front-back root spread, behind the trunk's broken oval end. Keep a true end-on trunk, not a long horizontal branch. The vertical fork appears above the end in RIGHT but becomes a short end-on stub/socket in TOP. Keep FRONT recognizable as the supplied object and match the location of every joint in all projections. Use light gray mass, thin dark contour and a few structural lines. No color, no bark texture, no painted lighting or cast shadow. No perspective, isometric, or three-quarter cameras. Do not add dimension numbers; the purpose is coherent projection, not invented measurements. Make the geometry internally consistent before adding fine details.

stages.notes: Pure-white validate must pass before trim/matte.
